claim_traces.claim_title: Humans only use 10% of their brains
claim_traces.claim_text: "Humans only use 10% of their brain capacity — the other 90% remains dormant and untapped."
reasoning_steps: Decades of rigorous neuroscience research have thoroughly debunked the assertion that humans only use 10% of their brains
Modern neuroimaging technologies, such as fMRI and PET scans, demonstrate that almost all areas of the brain are active during routine daily tasks, and even during sleep

Furthermore, any brain regions left genuinely unused due to injury or disease rapidly degrade (atrophy) or are repurposed, confirming that there is no dormant, untapped 90% of brain tissue in healthy individuals.

claim_traces.claim_title: Great Wall of China visible from space
claim_traces.claim_text: "The Great Wall of China is the only man-made structure visible from space with the naked eye."
reasoning_steps: Numerous astronauts, including China's own Yang Liwei, and space agencies like NASA have debunked this claim

The Great Wall is relatively narrow (usually less than 9 meters wide) and is constructed of materials that blend in color with the surrounding terrain, making it impossible to see with the naked eye from orbit without magnification

Additionally, other larger, high-contrast man-made structures (such as desert highways, airports, and large greenhouse complexes) are visible from low Earth orbit, meaning the Great Wall is neither visible nor unique in this regard.

claim_traces.claim_text: "Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short — around 5 feet 2 inches tall."
reasoning_steps: The claim that Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short and around 5 feet 2 inches tall is false
The height of 5 feet 2 inches was recorded in pre-metric French units (French feet and inches), which were longer than English units
In modern English measurements, Napoleon was actually about 5 feet 6 inches (or 1.68 meters) tall, which was average or even slightly above average for a French man of his era.

claim_traces.claim_text: "MSG (monosodium glutamate) causes headaches, numbness, and other symptoms — so-called 'Chinese restaurant syndrome.'"
reasoning_steps: The claim that MSG causes headaches, numbness, and 'Chinese restaurant syndrome' is misleading
While this belief was popularized after a 1968 letter to the New England Journal of Medicine, decades of subsequent scientific research have debunked it
Rigorous double-blind, placebo-controlled studies have failed to establish a consistent causal link between normal dietary MSG consumption and these symptoms

Additionally, the FDA classifies MSG as 'Generally Recognized as Safe' (GRAS), and the glutamate in MSG is chemically identical to the glutamate naturally present in foods like tomatoes and aged cheeses.

claim_traces.claim_title: Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood
claim_traces.claim_text: "Octopuses have three hearts and their blood is blue."
reasoning_steps: The claim is scientifically accurate

Octopuses have a closed circulatory system with three hearts: two branchial hearts that pump blood to the gills to absorb oxygen, and one systemic heart that pumps oxygenated blood to the rest of the body

Furthermore, their blood is blue because they use the copper-based protein hemocyanin to transport oxygen, which binds with oxygen and turns blue (becoming colorless when deoxygenated), unlike the iron-based hemoglobin found in vertebrates.

claim_traces.claim_title: The Moon is drifting away from Earth
claim_traces.claim_text: "The Moon is slowly moving away from Earth at a rate of about 3.8 centimeters per year."
reasoning_steps: The claim is scientifically accurate and widely accepted

Decades of precise measurements from the Lunar Laser Ranging experiment (which bounces lasers off retroreflectors left by Apollo astronauts) have established that the Moon is receding from Earth at a rate of approximately 3.78 centimeters (rounded to 3.8 cm) per year

This recession is caused by tidal friction, where the gravitational interaction between the Earth's oceans and the Moon transfers rotational energy from Earth into the Moon's orbital energy, pushing it into a higher orbit.
